notes:
Mercedes-Benz W169 A-Class (2004 to 2012) and W245 B-Class (2005 to 2011), engine only.

The engine control unit is the one unit any open source places: OBDb's 2011 A 180 capture has 0x7E0 answering service 22 (identifiers 0163, 0168 and 016F) with multi-frame replies on 0x7E8 on 11-bit CAN, and its 2009 capture has 0x7E0 answering OBD mode 01. The 2011 capture is from a diesel car (OBDb names the identifiers boost, exhaust back pressure and diesel particulate filter pressure, and fuel temperature); a petrol engine such as the M266 has a different controller and may answer differently.

Protocol and session: KWP2000 with session 0x92, as in the W211 profile. The basis is Xplatforms/mercedes-hacking-docs chapter 3, which lists the same wake-up frame for the W169 and W245 as for the W211 (ID 0x001C carrying `02 10 92`, a KWP2000 session start); that table is crowd-sourced, it is a broadcast on the interior bus rather than a request to the engine, and no source shows the engine accepting `10 92`, so the session is unverified. The bit rate is the 500 kbit/s that the sources in docs/vehicles/mercedes-benz.md give for CAN-C; OBDb's captures show 11-bit identifiers but do not state the rate, so that is unverified too.

Every other unit (transmission, ESP, airbags, cluster and the interior bus) is left out: no source gives W169 or W245 addresses for them (issue 88). Treat the engine row as unconfirmed on a given car until `obd-read probe` shows it answering. Sources and their limits are in docs/vehicles/mercedes-compact.md.
name: mercedes-w169-w245
